newsitem.title: USA: New Products - More baths spur new products.
newsitem.headline: New Products - More baths spur new products.

text.p: Bath-taking is on the rise. We're not talking quick showers. We're talking long, hot soaks.
Apparently, 23 percent of American women said recently they took a bath within the past 24 hours, up from 17 percent the prior year.

Because Americans are looking for a harmless and inexpensive respite from stress, they are taking to their tubs. New products for the bath are being introduced for this new (or old?) "lifestyle," says the New York-based research firm, Packaged Facts.
The market is growing, and the makers of bath and shower products saw product sales jump 82 percent between 1994 and 1996, to a value of about $921 million.

The bulk of growth in this market has been in the body wash category, and many top-selling, mass-retailed body washes, such as Lever Bros.'s Caress Moisturizing Body Wash and Procter & Gamble's Zest Family Deodorant Wash are extensions of established, branded soap lines.

In the future, Packaged Facts said in its industry report on the bath and shower care products market, "two-in-one" products will gain in popularity. Already, such products are making inroads, including products that combine body wash and moisturizer.

An up-and-coming trend will be deodorant body washes, with current offerings including products by Lever 2000 and Zest. Another double trend will be the inclusion of ingredients beneficial and restful to the skin and muscles.
Cabot Laboratories offers products that contain Dead Sea salts to ease tension and help tired muscles, and eucalyptus to soothe and purify the skin.

Also gaining in popularity is the inclusion of ingredients to help give a youthful appearance to the skin. Nivea extended its line last year with Nivea Shower & Bath Skin Renewal Gel with Alpha Hydroxy Acids.
"Whether or not the American obsession with staying young forces the introduction of more products containing anti-ageing ingredients remains to be seen," Packaged Facts said.
What moos like a cow, honks like a Model-T, rings like a bell and says "Nick Nick Nick"? Why, a telephone, of course.
The new TalkBlaster telephone by Long Hall Technologies, of Farmingdale, N.Y., is the latest addition to Nickelodeon's line of "serious electronics" for kids and families.

The TalkBlaster, a working telephone, has a "Green Slime" power rod that lights up when a call comes in. There is a redial button and the phone has five choices of rings -- moo, bell, honk, Nick Nick sound or a standard ring.
The phone also has a pulse/tone option and the receiver is hearing aid compatible.
Made from impact resistant plastic, the phone contains only child-safe inks, paints and other coatings.
The telephone joins other "Blaster" items including the BlastBox am/fm stereo casssette recorder and BlastPak personal am/fm stereo cassette player.
Each product in the Blaster line is reviewed and tested for child safety by Inchcape Testing Services and conforms with the U.S. Child Safety Standard ASTM F963, Long Hall said.
TalkBalster will be availabe beginning in May and will sell for about $49.95.
Gardening has become gender specific with a new line of gardening tools from UnionTools, called Lady Gardener Perfect Fit Gardening Tools.
The Columbus, Ohio-based company said the tools evolved from research that showed that women wanted garden equipment that was smaller, had slimmer handles, was lighter in weight and was attractive.
"Our research told us women wanted lawn and garden tools designed specifically for them," said Chuck Mattes, UnionTool's director of marketing.
"Based on their input, we've developed the industry's first line of tools that was literally designed by women -- for women," he said.

The Lady Gardener product line has 11 tools, including shovels, rakes and trowels. They range in price from $15 to $20, and are being introduced into mass market retailers, home stores and hardware stores.
For more information, the company can be reached at 614-222-4400.
